questions.problem:
Consider the change of variables given by the matrix equation

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} & -\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} \\ \frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}],
$$

and the curve $C,$ defined as

$$
C:\,2{x}_{1}^{2}+4{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+5{x}_{2}^{2}+4\sqrt{5}{x}_{1}-2\sqrt{5}{x}_{2}=-26.
$$

 

Given that the change of variables above reduces $Q(x)=2{x}_{1}^{2}+4{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+5{x}_{2}^{2}$ to its canonical (diagonal) form $6{y}_{1}^{2}+{y}_{2}^{2},$ what type of a quadratic curve is defined by $C?$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we note the following:

$$
C:\,{{2{x}_{1}^{2}+4{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+5{x}_{2}^{2}}_{⏟}}_{Q(x)}+4\sqrt{5}{x}_{1}-2\sqrt{5}{x}_{2}=-26
$$

Let's write the given change of variables explicitly:

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} & -\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} \\ \frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}]\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}{y}_{1}-\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}{y}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}=\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}{y}_{1}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}{y}_{2},\end{aligned}
$$

We know that the given change of variables reduces $Q(x)$ to its canonical form. Therefore, performing the change of variables on $C,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}^{2}+4{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+5{x}_{2}^{2}+4\sqrt{5}{x}_{1}-2\sqrt{5}{x}_{2} & =-26 \\ 6{y}_{1}^{2}+{y}_{2}^{2}+4\sqrt{5}(\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}{y}_{1}-\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}{y}_{2})-2\sqrt{5}(\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}{y}_{1}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}{y}_{2}) & =-26 \\ 6{y}_{1}^{2}+{y}_{2}^{2}-10{y}_{2} & =-26\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we complete the square for the variable ${y}_{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}6{y}_{1}^{2}+{y}_{2}^{2}-10{y}_{2} & =-26 \\ 6{y}_{1}^{2}+({y}_{2}^{2}-10{y}_{2}+25)-25 & =-26 \\ 6{y}_{1}^{2}+{({y}_{2}-5)}^{2}-25 & =-26 \\ 6{y}_{1}^{2}+{({y}_{2}-5)}^{2} & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, performing the change of variables

$$
{\begin{aligned}{z}_{1}={y}_{1}, \\ {z}_{2}={y}_{2}-5,\end{aligned}
$$

 

we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}6{z}_{1}^{2}+{z}_{2}^{2} & =-1 \\ \frac{{z}_{1}^{2}}{(\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}})^{2}}+{z}_{2}^{2} & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

 

This defines an empty set, also called an imaginary ellipse. Notice that the left-hand side is non-negative for all ${z}_{1}$ and ${z}_{2},$ while the right-hand side is negative.

questions.problem:
What type of quadratic curve is defined by the following equation?

$$
{x}_{1}^{2}-4{x}_{1}=-5
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we complete the squares for the variable ${x}_{1}:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{2}-4{x}_{1} & =-5 \\ ({x}_{1}^{2}-4{x}_{1}+4)-4 & =-5 \\ ({x}_{1}-2)^{2} & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

Now, performing the change of variable

$$
{y}_{1}={x}_{1}-2,\,
$$

we get the equation

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{1}^{2} & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

 
which defines an empty set. Notice that the left-hand side is non-negative for all ${y}_{1}$ while the right-hand side is negative. In this case, we say that the equation represents a pair of imaginary parallel lines.

choices.value: A pair of imaginary parallel lines

answer_fields.correct_value: A pair of imaginary parallel lines

questions.problem:
What type of quadratic curve is defined by the following equation?

$$
{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}^{2}-4{x}_{2}=0
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we complete the squares for the variable ${x}_{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}^{2}-4{x}_{2} & =0 \\ {x}_{1}+2({x}_{2}^{2}-2{x}_{2}) & =0 \\ {x}_{1}+2({x}_{2}^{2}-2{x}_{2}+1-1) & =0 \\ {x}_{1}+2({x}_{2}-1)^{2}-2 & =0 \\ 2({x}_{2}-1)^{2} & =-({x}_{1}-2)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, performing the change of variables

$$
{\begin{aligned}{y}_{1}={x}_{1}-2, \\ {y}_{2}={x}_{2}-1,\end{aligned}
$$

we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}2{y}_{2}^{2} & =-{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}^{2} & =-\frac{1}{2}{y}_{1}\end{aligned}
$$

 

This represents a parabola that opens in the direction of the negative ${y}_{1}$-axis.

questions.problem:
Consider the change of variables given by the matrix equation

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{5} & \frac{4}{5} \\ \frac{4}{5} & -\frac{3}{5}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}],
$$

and the curve $C,$ defined as

$$
C:\,11{x}_{1}^{2}-24{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+4{x}_{2}^{2}+12{x}_{1}+16{x}_{2}=20.
$$

Given that the change of variables above reduces $Q(x)=11{x}_{1}^{2}-24{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+4{x}_{2}^{2}$ to its canonical (diagonal) form $20{y}_{2}^{2}-5{y}_{1}^{2}$ what type of a quadratic curve is defined by $C?$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we note the following:

$$
C:\,{{11{x}_{1}^{2}-24{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+4{x}_{2}^{2}}_{⏟}}_{Q(x)}+12{x}_{1}+16{x}_{2}=20
$$

Let's write the given change of variables explicitly:

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{5} & \frac{4}{5} \\ \frac{4}{5} & -\frac{3}{5}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}]\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}=\frac{3}{5}{y}_{1}+\frac{4}{5}{y}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}=\frac{4}{5}{y}_{1}-\frac{3}{5}{y}_{2},\end{aligned}
$$

We know that the given change of variables reduces $Q(x)$ to its canonical form. Therefore, performing the change of variables on $C,$ we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}11{x}_{1}^{2}-24{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+4{x}_{2}^{2}+12{x}_{1}+16{x}_{2} & =20 \\ 20{y}_{2}^{2}-5{y}_{1}^{2}+12(\frac{3}{5}{y}_{1}+\frac{4}{5}{y}_{2})+16(\frac{4}{5}{y}_{1}-\frac{3}{5}{y}_{2}) & =20 \\ 20{y}_{2}^{2}-5{y}_{1}^{2}+20{y}_{1} & =20.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we complete the square for the variable ${y}_{1}:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}20{y}_{2}^{2}-5{y}_{1}^{2}+20{y}_{1} & =20 \\ 4{y}_{2}^{2}-{y}_{1}^{2}+4{y}_{1} & =4 \\ 4{y}_{2}^{2}-({y}_{1}^{2}-4{y}_{1}+4-4) & =4 \\ 4{y}_{2}^{2}-({y}_{1}-2)^{2}+4 & =4 \\ 4{y}_{2}^{2}-({y}_{1}-2)^{2} & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, performing the change of variables 

$$
{\begin{aligned}{z}_{1}={y}_{1}-2, \\ {z}_{2}={y}_{2},\end{aligned}
$$

we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}4{y}_{2}^{2}-({y}_{1}-2)^{2} & =0 \\ 4{z}_{2}^{2}-{z}_{1}^{2} & =0\end{aligned}
$$

 

This represents the pair of intersecting lines ${z}_{1}=2{z}_{2}$ and ${z}_{1}=-2{z}_{2}.$
